data.title: A statement on the so-called “Slavic-Aryan Vedas”
data.excerpt: The plague known as the Slavic-Aryan Vedas has been on our radar for some time, but their theories are so foolish that writing about them would mean wasting precious time on studying nonsense. Žiarislav has now published a clear and uncompromising statement about them, and we agree with most of what he says.
data.metaDescription: Why the so-called Slavic-Aryan Vedas are pseudo-historical nonsense — a critical statement on this widespread mystification of the history of the Slavs.

mediaTexts.alt: A fantasy painting of flying machines above a Slavic landscape with figures in period dress

children.text: The plague known as the Slavic-Aryan Vedas has been on our radar for quite some time. Their theories are so foolish that I have never been able to bring myself to write anything meaningful about them. That would require me to spend a fairly considerable amount of time studying the nonsense they preach, and my time is too precious for that.

I was all the more pleased that this thankless task has been taken on by Žiarislav, who today published on his website a clear and uncompromising statement on the so-called “Slavic-Aryan Vedas”. Since I identify with most of the positions he expresses in that statement, I consider it necessary to draw the attention of our readers to his article too, in which he explains to readers briefly and comprehensibly where the danger of this foolish modern ideology lies, an ideology that literally sabotages and discredits the history of the Slavs and of the people who want to devote themselves to it. So let us let Žiarislav speak for himself:

blocks.alt: A statement on the so-called "Slavic-Aryan Vedas"

children.text: "A declaration on the "Slavic-Aryan Vedas". (Click on the article below.) So that it is clear who is who. Somebody said – surely you are after the same thing. But that is not true. We have neither common means nor common aims. All sorts of people hide behind Slavdom nowadays. Many abuse it, they abuse national feeling and in this way they dishonour genuine Slavic spirituality. The essence of vedomectvo (the way of knowing) is knowledge, that is, awareness, good seeing – "návisť". And it cannot be the other way round. Perhaps, if we say things clearly and truthfully, we shall lose a few friends – but were they then really our friends? We shall gain more. We shall be closer to the truth and our friendships will be more genuine. If we want to cultivate respect, we must also keep our honour. And speak about things purely and clearly, as we see them. So be it.

With a great deal of hatred, arrogance and above all speculative interpretation, invention and distortion of the facts, the groups spreading the so-called “Slavic-Aryan Vedas” in the Slavic countries have managed partly to discredit the original Slavic cultural currents, which less well-informed people are unable to tell apart from them."
